title: Direct vs Oblique Personal Pronouns
subtitle: Distinguish between caseless subjects and oblique pronouns for objects and possession
keyPoint: Direct pronouns mark subjects in present tense, while oblique pronouns mark objects, possessors, and prepositional complements.

cells: we, you, they / us, you, them

mistakes.note: Present tense subjects require direct case (ez), not oblique (min).

mistakes.wrong: Pirtûka ez li ser maseyê ye.
mistakes.right: Pirtûka min li ser maseyê ye.
mistakes.note: Possession requires the oblique pronoun (min) after the ezafe.
In the present tense, direct objects must take the oblique case (te).

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun for: '___ go to work every day.' (I)
quiz.explanation: 'Ez' is the 1st person singular direct pronoun required for present tense subjects.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun for: 'This is ___ book.' (her)
quiz.explanation: The feminine 3rd person singular oblique pronoun 'wê' marks possession.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun for: 'Do you see ___?' (him)
quiz.explanation: 'Wî' is the masculine singular oblique pronoun used for direct objects in present tense.

quiz.question: Choose the correct pronoun for: 'The teacher called ___.' (us)
quiz.explanation: 'Me' is the 1st person plural oblique pronoun used as an object.

tip: Always use 'ez, tu, ew' to do the action now, and 'min, te, wî/wê' when someone or something receives the action or owns something.

title: Present Copula Enclitic Endings
subtitle: Form sentences with the bound present 'to be' endings
keyPoint: The Kurdish present tense verb 'to be' attaches directly to nouns and adjectives as an enclitic personal suffix.

mistakes.note: The 1st person singular copula after a vowel is 'me', not 'e'.
Use singular '-e' for 'he/she is'; '-in' is reserved for plural subjects.
Match 2nd person pronoun 'tu' with the 2nd person enclitic '-î'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ez xwendekar ___.' (I am a student)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular copula after a consonant is '-im'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ew mamoste ___.' (She is a teacher)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular copula after a vowel is 'ye'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Em heval ___.' (We are friends)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural takes the copula suffix '-in' after a consonant.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Tu pir jîr ___.' (You are very smart)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular pronoun 'tu' requires the suffix '-î'.

tip: If the preceding word ends in a vowel, use the forms starting with 'y' or 'm/n' (me, yî, ye, ne) to prevent vowel clash.

title: The Basic Ezafe Construction
subtitle: Connect nouns to adjectives and possessors using gendered linkers
keyPoint: The Ezafe suffix attaches to a noun to link it with an adjective or possessor, reflecting the noun's gender and number.

mistakes.wrong: Pirtûkê min li ser maseyê ye.
mistakes.right: Pirtûka min li ser maseyê ye.
mistakes.note: 'Pirtûk' (book) is grammatically feminine, so it takes the feminine ezafe '-a'.

mistakes.wrong: Hevala baş hat (referring to male friend).
mistakes.note: Use masculine ezafe '-ê' for masculine nouns like male friend.
'Zarokên' is plural, requiring the plural copula 'in' instead of singular 'e'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for: 'the big house' ('mal' is feminine): 'Mal___ mezin.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns take the '-a' ezafe suffix.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for: 'the brother of Azad' ('bira' is masculine, vowel-ending): 'Bira___ Azad.'
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns ending in a vowel take the '-yê' ezafe connector.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for: 'the new books' ('pirtûk' in plural): 'Pirtûk___ nû.'
quiz.explanation: All plural nouns take '-ên' (or '-yên' after vowels) in the ezafe construction.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for: 'the fast car' ('erebe' is feminine, vowel-ending): 'Erebe___ lez.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns ending in a vowel take '-ya'.

tip: Think of the ezafe like an apostrophe-S or 'of': it glues a description or an owner directly to the noun.

title: Grammatical Gender and Demonstratives
subtitle: Master masculine and feminine noun distinctions with demonstratives
keyPoint: All Kurdish singular nouns are either masculine or feminine, which dictates demonstrative oblique forms and vocative/ezafe agreements.

examples.en: Ez ji vî bajarî hez dikim.
Ew kinc li ser wê kursiyê ye.

mistakes.note: 'Kur' (boy) is masculine; it requires the masculine demonstrative 'vî'.

mistakes.wrong: Ew li vî bajêr dijî (referring to female city/noun).
mistakes.note: 'Bajar' is masculine, so 'vî' is correct, but remember feminine nouns take 'vê'.

mistakes.wrong: Ez hez ji ev xanî dikim.
mistakes.right: Ez hez ji vî xanî dikim.
mistakes.note: Prepositions trigger the oblique case; demonstrative 'ev' must become 'vî' or 'vê'.

quiz.question: Choose the oblique near demonstrative for feminine noun 'jin' (woman): 'Ez ___ jinê nas dikim.'
quiz.explanation: 'Vê' is the feminine singular oblique near demonstrative.

quiz.question: Choose the oblique near demonstrative for masculine noun 'xort' (young man): 'Ez ___ xortî dibînim.'
quiz.explanation: 'Vî' is the masculine singular oblique near demonstrative.

quiz.question: Choose the oblique plural demonstrative for: 'We see ___ children.'
quiz.explanation: 'Van' is the oblique plural form of 'ev' (these).

quiz.question: Choose the oblique far demonstrative for masculine noun 'mêr' (man): 'Ez bi ___ re dipeyivim.'
quiz.explanation: 'Wî' is the masculine singular oblique far demonstrative.

tip: Most biological females, abstract concepts, tools, and nature words tend to be feminine (mê), while biological males and seasons are masculine (nêr).

title: Present Continuous/Indicative with Di-
subtitle: Construct present affirmative actions using prefix di- and personal endings
keyPoint: The present tense is formed by placing the prefix 'di-' before the present verbal stem and appending subject agreement endings.

mistakes.note: The affirmative present indicative requires the aspectual prefix 'di-'.
Match 2nd person subject 'tu' with personal ending '-î', not 1st person '-im'.
Plural subjects take the suffix '-in', contracted with stem 'ç-' to become 'diçin'.

quiz.question: Complete the verb: 'Ez pirtûkekê di-nivîs-___.' (I write a book)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular ending for verbs in the present tense is '-im'.

quiz.question: Complete the verb: 'Ew çayê di-xw-___.' (She drinks/eats tea)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular present personal ending is '-e'.

quiz.question: Complete the verb: 'Tu pir baş di-peyiv-___.' (You speak very well)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular personal ending is '-î'.

quiz.question: Complete the verb: 'Em kurdî di-bêj-___.' (We speak/say Kurdish)
quiz.explanation: All plural persons (em, hûn, ew) take the ending '-in'.

tip: Formula: Subject + di- + Present Stem + Personal Suffix (-im, -î, -e, -in).

title: Verbal Negation with Ne-, Na-, and Nî-
subtitle: Master the essential negative prefixes across tenses and copulas
keyPoint: Use na- for present indicative verbs, ne- for past tenses and non-indicative moods, and nî- exclusively to negate the present copula.

useCases.label: Negating Present Identity or State
useCases.example: Ev pirtûk ne ya min e, ew nîne.

mistakes.note: Use na- instead of ne- for present tense verbs, and keep the verb at the end.

mistakes.wrong: Ew îro li vir ne ye.
mistakes.note: The negative copula in the third person singular combines into nîne rather than ne ye.
Simple past verbs must be negated with ne-, never with the present prefix na-.

quiz.question: How do you say 'I do not drink tea' in the present tense? 'Ez çayê ___.'
quiz.explanation: The present continuous/habitual prefix di- is replaced by the negative prefix na-, yielding venaxwim.

quiz.question: How do you say 'They did not come yesterday'? 'Duh ew ___.'
quiz.explanation: The simple past requires the prefix ne- combined with the third-person plural ending -in, giving nehatin.

quiz.question: How do you say 'He is not at home right now'? 'Ew niha li malê ___.'
quiz.explanation: The negative 3rd person singular present copula meaning 'is not' is nîne.

quiz.question: How do you say 'We do not know'? 'Em ___.'
quiz.explanation: The verb zanîn (to know) uses the irregular present negative stem nizan-, giving nizanin for 'we do not know'.

tip: Remember that the present tense affirmative marker di- completely disappears when na- is attached, so dixwim becomes naxwim.

title: Simple Past Conjugation of Intransitive Verbs
subtitle: Conjugate verbs of motion and state using direct case pronouns
keyPoint: Intransitive verbs in the past tense take direct case subjects and agree directly in person and number with the verb suffix.

useCases.label: Describing Movements Completed in the Past
Reporting Arrival and Departure
useCases.example: Mêvan saet di heştan de hatin.

examples.en: Xwişka min duh ji zanîngehê zivirî.
Ew hemû li ber derî man.

mistakes.note: Intransitive past verbs require the direct subject pronoun (Ez), not the oblique pronoun (Min).
If the subject is singular (hevalê min), the verb takes zero suffix in the 3rd person singular, not the plural -in.
The second person singular pronoun tu requires the agreement suffix -î or -yî.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Duh şev ez pir dereng ___.' (I slept)
quiz.explanation: The direct subject ez requires the 1st person singular past suffix -m, giving razam.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Gelo hûn çima ne___?' (Why didn't you plural come?)
quiz.explanation: Plural subjects (em, hûn, ew) always take the suffix -n in the simple past, forming nehatin.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Duh hevala min zû ___.' (My friend left/went)
quiz.explanation: A singular 3rd person subject (hevala min) takes no suffix on the past stem, so çû is correct.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses an intransitive verb in the simple past?
quiz.explanation: Ez çûm malê uses the direct pronoun ez with the correct 1st person past agreement suffix -m.

tip: To find any verb's past stem, simply remove the infinitive suffix -in or -an: e.g., hatin → hat-, ketin → ket-.

title: Circumpositional Adpositions and the Oblique Case
subtitle: Master Kurdish bracket prepositions like li... de and ji... re
keyPoint: Circumpositions enclose nouns that must take oblique case inflection, marking exact spatial and directional relations.

useCases.label: Expressing an Addressee or Beneficiary
useCases.example: Wî ji dayika xwe re got.

useCases.label: Expressing Accompaniment
useCases.example: Ew bi birayê xwe re dimeşe.

examples.en: Pirtûk li ser masê de nîne.
Ew her roj bi hevalê xwe re dipeyive.
Min ji xwişka xwe re nameyek şand.
Zarok di nav baxçeyî de dileyizin.
Diz di pencereya mezin re reviya.

mistakes.note: Personal pronouns enclosed by adpositions must take their oblique form (min, not ez).
Feminine singular nouns enclosed by prepositions must take the oblique ending -ê.
Masculine nouns ending in consonants or undergoing internal vowel harmony must show oblique inflection.

quiz.question: Choose the right pronoun: 'Ew dixwaze bi ___ re biçe sînemayê.' (with you [singular])
quiz.explanation: Circumpositions require the oblique case; the oblique form of 'tu' is 'te'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'in the room' (ode - fem.): 'Ew li ___ de rûniştiye.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns take the oblique ending -ê (with glide -y- after a vowel), resulting in odeyê.

quiz.question: How do you say 'He told me' using the benefactive/recipient circumposition? 'Ew ji ___ re got.'
quiz.explanation: The recipient takes ji... re with the first-person singular oblique pronoun min.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Zarok bi diya xwe ___ dimeşin.'
quiz.explanation: The preposition bi pairs with the postposition re to denote accompaniment ('together with').

tip: Think of circumpositions as verbal bookends: the first element indicates the basic relationship, while the final particle reinforces orientation or completion.

title: Imperative and Prohibitive Moods with Bi- and Me-
subtitle: Issue direct commands and prohibitions using present roots
keyPoint: Form positive imperatives using the modal prefix bi- on the present stem, and form negative commands (prohibitions) by replacing bi- with me-.

useCases.label: Giving Direct Instructions
useCases.example: Ji kerema xwe re derî veke!

examples.en: Hûn li ser vê kursiyê rûnenên!
Rastiyê ji hevalên xwe re bibêje!
Ji vir derkevin û herin malê!

mistakes.note: Imperative commands use the prohibitive prefix me-, not the indicative past negation prefix ne-.
Singular commands to one person end in -e or bare stem; -in is reserved for plural addressees.
Compound verbs with prefixes (like der-) drop the imperative marker bi- completely.

quiz.question: How do you order a single person: 'Speak!' (axaftin, present stem: axiv-)?
quiz.explanation: The singular imperative is formed by attaching bi- to the present root along with the singular ending -e: biaxive.

quiz.question: How do you tell a group: 'Do not go!' (çûn, stem: ç-)?
quiz.explanation: Prohibitions for plural audiences use the prefix me- followed by stem and the plural suffix -in: meçin.

quiz.question: How do you tell someone: 'Do not do that!' (kirin, stem: k-)?
quiz.explanation: The negative imperative for kirin in singular is meke.

quiz.question: What happens to the prefix 'bi-' when the verb already has a spatial prefix like 've-' (vekirin)?
quiz.explanation: Preverbal spatial prefixes (like ve-, der-, hil-) displace and drop the imperative prefix bi-.

tip: Listen for colloquial speech where me- sometimes softens into ne-, but in standard written Kurdish, me- is required for all prohibitions.

title: Indefinite Nominal Suffixes (-ek and -in)
subtitle: Form indefinite nouns and link them accurately with Ezafe
keyPoint: Attach -ek to singular nouns for indefinite reference ('a/an') and link adjectives with the indefinite Ezafe marker -e.

examples.en: Ew keçeke pir jîr û delal e.
Li ser sifrê sêvek sor heye.

mistakes.wrong: Yek pirtûk li ser masê ye.
mistakes.note: Rather than placing the numeral yek before nouns for general 'a/an', attach the suffix -ek to the noun.
An indefinite feminine noun followed by an adjective requires the indefinite Ezafe connector -e (-eke total).
Masculine indefinite nouns taking an adjective must use the connector -î (-ekî total), not the bare suffix.

quiz.question: How do you say 'a woman' (jin)?
quiz.explanation: The standard singular indefinite suffix is -ek, yielding jinek.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'a good boy' (kur - masc.):
quiz.explanation: Masculine nouns marked with -ek take the indefinite Ezafe connector -î before an adjective: kurekî baş.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'a beautiful city' (bajar - masc.):
quiz.explanation: Bajar is masculine, so it takes the masculine indefinite Ezafe -ekî before the adjective xweşik.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'a new car' (erebe - fem.):
quiz.explanation: Erebe ends in a vowel and is feminine, requiring the glide and feminine indefinite Ezafe -yeke before the adjective.

tip: Remember the gender difference in indefinite Ezafe: masculine nouns use -ekî (kurekî baş) while feminine nouns use -eke (keçeke baş).

title: Vocative Case Endings
subtitle: Addressing people directly in Kurdish
keyPoint: Add the suffix -o to call a masculine person, -ê to call a feminine person, and -ino to address a group directly.

mistakes.note: Use -o for masculine nouns; -ê is reserved exclusively for feminine nouns.
When addressing multiple people, use the plural vocative suffix -ino instead of singular -o.
Do not confuse the feminine oblique ending -ê with the vocative -ê; vocative is strictly for calling someone directly.

quiz.question: How do you call out to a young boy (kurik)?
quiz.explanation: Masculine singular nouns take the vocative suffix -o.

quiz.question: How do you address your sister (xwişk) directly?
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns take the vocative suffix -ê.

quiz.question: How do you get the attention of a group of students (xwendekar)?
quiz.explanation: Plural nouns take the vocative suffix -ino (or -no after vowels).

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly calls an uncle (xal)?
quiz.explanation: Xal is masculine, so it takes the -o vocative ending.

tip: If a word ends in a vowel, the vocative suffix often contracts or takes a glide, like 'bira' becoming 'biro'.

title: Basic Subjunctive with Modals
subtitle: Expressing ability, desire, and necessity
keyPoint: Modal verbs like karîn, xwestin, and divê trigger the dependent verb in the present subjunctive, usually marked by the bi- prefix.

examples.en: Ez dixwazim zimanê kurdî hîn bibim.
Ew dikarin bi me re bimeşin.
Gelo hûn dikarin vî karî çêbikin?

mistakes.note: The secondary verb must take the subjunctive prefix bi-, not the indicative prefix di-.
Impersonal modal 'divê' always requires the subjunctive mood on the following verb.
Double negation is ungrammatical; the negative modal 'nikare' already negates the phrase.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Ez dixwazim nan ___.' (xwarin)
quiz.explanation: The first person singular subjunctive form of xwarin is bixwim.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Divê tu zû ___.' (hatin)
quiz.explanation: Hatin has an irregular subjunctive stem; 2nd person singular is bêyî (or werî).

quiz.question: Complete: 'Ew dikarin bi kurdî ___.' (axaftin)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person plural ending is -in, giving biaxivin in the subjunctive.

quiz.question: Which sentence means 'We must study'?
quiz.explanation: Divê + subjunctive (bixebitin) expresses 'must study'.

tip: Compound verbs that use kirin or bûn drop the prefix bi- and instead conjugate the light verb directly as bikim, bibim, etc.

title: Split Ergativity in Past Tenses
subtitle: How Kurdish flips subject and object roles in the past
keyPoint: In past transitive sentences, the agent stands in the oblique case while the verb agrees exclusively with the direct-case object.

cells: Min, Te, Wî, Wê, Me, We, Wan
Ez, Tu, Ew, Em, Hûn, Ew
Ez çûm, Tu çûyî, Ew çû

mistakes.note: The agent of a transitive past action must be in the oblique case (min, not ez).
If the object 'ew' is singular, the verb must end with the 3rd person singular zero-ending (dît), not plural (-in).
Ergativity only applies to transitive verbs. 'Çûn' is intransitive, so the subject stays in the direct case (Ez).

quiz.question: Choose the correct agent: '___ sêv xwar.' (I ate an apple)
quiz.explanation: In past transitive clauses, the subject takes the oblique case 'min'.

quiz.question: Complete the verb: 'Wî em ___.' (He saw us)
quiz.explanation: The verb agrees with the direct-case object 'em' (we), taking the plural suffix -in.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Wê ez ___.' (She saw me)
quiz.explanation: The verb agrees with 'ez' (1st person singular), taking the suffix -im.

quiz.question: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
quiz.explanation: 'Wan' is oblique agent, 'nan' is singular direct object, so the verb 'xwar' is singular.

tip: Always identify whether the verb is transitive before speaking in the past; if it can take a direct object, use min/te/wî/wê/me/we/wan for the doer!

title: Past Continuous and Habitual Aspect
subtitle: Narrating ongoing or repeated events in the past
keyPoint: Prefixing di- to the simple past stem creates the past continuous/habitual tense, still obeying split-ergative rules for transitive verbs.

cells: I was going / used to go to school
I was reading / used to read books

useCases.label: Ongoing Background Action
useCases.example: Dema ew hat, min nan dixwar.

useCases.label: Childhood Habitual Event
useCases.example: Wê demê em her roj dilîstin.

examples.en: Dema tu hatî, min name dinivîsand.
Ew nedixwestin bi me re bipeyivin.

mistakes.note: Çûn is intransitive; do not use the oblique agent min even in the past continuous.
Past continuous requires the di- aspectual prefix; without it, it is a simple past attempt.
The negative marker merges with the aspectual prefix as nedi-, not separated.

quiz.question: Complete for 'I was walking': 'Ez hêdî hêdî ___.' (meşîn)
quiz.explanation: Intransitive past continuous: prefix di- + past stem meşiya- + 1st person ending -m.

quiz.question: Complete: 'Dema bavê min hat, me nan ___.' (xwarin)
quiz.explanation: The action of eating bread was ongoing in the past, requiring dixwar (agreeing with singular nan).

quiz.question: How do you say 'He used to not listen'?
quiz.explanation: The negation of compound past continuous joins as 'neguhdarî dikir' (or 'guhdarî nedikir').

quiz.question: What is the past habitual of 'Ew dibêjin' (They say)?
quiz.explanation: Gotin is transitive; in the past habitual with a singular omitted speech object, it is 'Wan digot'.

tip: Remember: The prefix 'di-' serves two roles—present indicative with present stems, and past continuous/habitual with past stems!

title: Compound Verbs with Kirin and Bûn
subtitle: Building active and stative actions with light verbs
keyPoint: Most modern Kurdish verbs are compounds made of a noun or adjective plus 'kirin' (to do/make, active) or 'bûn' (to become, passive/stative).

cells: to heat up vs to get warm
to clean vs to get cleaned

useCases.label: Inchoative / Becoming
useCases.example: Av di zivistanê de sar dibe.

examples.en: Ew her roj malê paqij dikin.

mistakes.note: Çêbûn is intransitive (to happen/be made); to express building something actively, use çêkirin.
The idiom 'to use' is 'bi kar anîn', requiring the preposition 'bi'.
If the subject grew up by itself without an external object, use bûn instead of kirin.

quiz.question: How do you say 'We cleaned the car'?
quiz.explanation: Paqij kirin is transitive; in past tense, agent is oblique (me) and verb is 'kir'.

quiz.question: What is the meaning of 'şiyar bûn'?
quiz.explanation: Compounds with 'bûn' are intransitive/reflexive: şiyar bûn = to wake up (oneself).

quiz.question: Which verb forms 'to start' transitively (e.g. to start a class)?
quiz.explanation: 'Dest pê kirin' is transitive 'to start (something)', whereas 'dest pê bûn' is intransitive.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Av zû kel ___.' (The water boiled)
quiz.explanation: 'Kel bûn' means to boil intransitively; in simple past it becomes 'kel bû'.

tip: Pairing rule: Whenever you see an unfamiliar adjective, you can usually turn it into a verb immediately by appending 'kirin' (to make it X) or 'bûn' (to become X)!

title: Present Perfect and Pluperfect Formations
subtitle: Expressing actions completed before the present or prior to another past event
keyPoint: The present perfect attaches clitic copular suffixes to the past stem, while the pluperfect adds the past auxiliary bûyîn.

cells: I have gone to the city.

useCases.label: Prior Past Completion
useCases.example: Dema ew hat, min xwarin xwaribû.

mistakes.note: Transitive verbs in perfect tenses require the subject to be in the oblique case due to ergative alignment.
The pluperfect auxiliary agrees with the direct object (here third-person singular), not the agent.
The third person singular present perfect suffix is attached directly as -ye to stems ending in vowels.

quiz.question: Complete with present perfect: 'I have arrived home.' -> 'Ez gihîştime ___.'
quiz.explanation: Nouns of destination take the oblique ending (-ê for feminine nouns like mal).

quiz.question: Choose the correct pluperfect form: 'She had already bought the car.' -> 'Wê erebe berê ___.'
quiz.explanation: The pluperfect of kirîn (to buy) matching a singular feminine direct object is kiribû.

quiz.question: Which sentence contains a present perfect transitive verb?
quiz.explanation: 'Min nan xwariye' features an ergative subject (min) and present perfect verb (xwariye).

quiz.question: Identify the incorrect agreement in the pluperfect:
quiz.explanation: The transitive verb agrees with the plural object 'sê sêv', so it must be xwaribûn, not xwaribûm.

tip: Remember that in both present perfect and pluperfect, transitive verbs agree in person and number with the grammatical patient (object), never the agent!

title: Passive Construction with Hatin + Infinitive
subtitle: Using the auxiliary hatin with oblique verbal nouns to form passives
keyPoint: The passive voice is formed by conjugating the auxiliary verb hatin to match the patient, followed by the oblique infinitive (-inê/-anê) of the main verb.

useCases.label: Unspecified Agent Events
useCases.example: Diz di şevê de hat girtinê.

examples.en: Dergeh di saet heştan de tê vekirinê.
Ew xanî sala borî hat firotinê.
Name ji aliyê bavê min ve hatiye xwendinê.
Projeya nû wê zû bê temamkirinê.

mistakes.note: In standard Kurmanji passive structures, the infinitive must receive the oblique suffix -ê.
The auxiliary verb hatin must conjugate to agree with the subject in person and number (ez hatim).
Passive subjects are patients; do not keep the original active agent as the grammatical subject.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form: 'The letters were written.' -> 'Name ___ nivîsandinê.'
quiz.explanation: The subject 'name' is plural here ('letters'), so hatin agrees with the plural subject in the past.

quiz.question: How do you say 'Bread is eaten every morning'?
quiz.explanation: Present tense singular passive requires 'tê' followed by the oblique infinitive 'xwarinê'.

quiz.question: Which verb acts as the passive auxiliary in Kurmanji?
quiz.explanation: The auxiliary verb 'hatin' (to come) is uniquely used to form analytic passive constructions.

quiz.question: Select the correct future passive: 'The bridge will be repaired.'
quiz.explanation: 'wê bê' marks the future passive singular corresponding to 'will be'.

tip: To specify the agent in a passive sentence, use the circumposition 'ji aliyê ... ve' (e.g., ji aliyê polîsan ve = by the police).

title: Morphological Causatives (-andin / -andin)
subtitle: Deriving transitive and causative verbs from intransitive stems and adjectives
keyPoint: Appending the suffix -andin to an intransitive root or adjective base converts it into a transitive or causative verb stem.

useCases.label: Making Someone Do Something
useCases.example: Mamoste şagirt da axaftinê lê wî ders fêhmand.

useCases.label: Direct Causation from Adjectives
useCases.example: Dê şîr ji bo zarokê xwe germand.

useCases.label: Transitivizing Motion Verbs
useCases.example: Şofêr erebeyê li dora bajêr digerîne.

examples.en: Wî zarok ji xewê hişyar kir û tirsand.
Ew kevirê giran bi hêsanî dihejîne.
Wan xaniyê kevn bi temamî şewitandin.
Karker daran li erdê dirêj dikin û dirizînin.
Dayikê pitika xwe di landikê de hejand.

mistakes.note: Şewitîn is intransitive ('catches fire'); şewitandin with present stem -şewitîn- is needed for transitive burning.
Tirsîn is intransitive ('to be afraid'); the transitive causative counterpart is tirsandin ('to scare').
Adjectives take causative suffixes (-andin) or verbalizers like kirin to produce transitive actions.

quiz.question: What is the causative counterpart of the intransitive verb 'firin' (to fly)?
quiz.explanation: The causative suffix -andin attaches to the root 'fir-', giving 'firandin' (to make fly / launch).

quiz.question: In the present tense, causatives in -andin change their suffix to:
quiz.explanation: The present stem for verbs in -andin regularizes with an -în- infix followed by personal endings (e.g., di-tirs-în-e).

quiz.question: Identify the causative transitive verb in this sentence: 'He scared the birds.'
quiz.explanation: 'Tirsandin' is the causative transitive form meaning 'to frighten/scare'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'Min şîr li ser sobeyê ___.' (I warmed up the milk.)
quiz.explanation: 'germand' is the simple past tense of the derived causative verb germandin (to heat).

tip: Notice the symmetry: intransitive past stems end in -î- (tirsî = was scared), while causative transitive past stems end in -and- (tirsand = scared someone).

title: Past Subjunctive and Counterfactual Conditionals
subtitle: Formulating impossible past conditions and hypothetical irrealis scenarios
keyPoint: Counterfactual conditionals combine the past conditional particle ba with past stems to express unreal past hypotheses.

cells: Had he not gone to town...
I wish I had been there!

useCases.label: Unfulfilled Past Hypotheses
useCases.example: Heke baran nebariya, em ê biçûna seyranê.

useCases.label: Expressing Past Regret
useCases.example: Xwezî min ew pirtûk zûtir bixwenda.

useCases.label: Imagined Alternatives
useCases.example: Ku te pere daban min, min ê erebeyek bikiriya.

examples.en: Heke te rastî bigota min, ez ê aciz nebûma.
Ku ew zû bihata, em ê negihîştina trênê.
Xwezî me bi hev re ev pirsgirêk çareser bikira.
Heke wan em vexwendibana, em ê bê guman biçûna.
Ku min bizaniba, min ê tu carî wusa nekira.

mistakes.wrong: Heke tu bê, ez ê kêfxweş bûma.
mistakes.right: Heke tu bihata, ez ê kêfxweş bibûma.
mistakes.note: Counterfactual past conditions require past subjunctive forms with -ba, not present subjunctive verbs like bê.

mistakes.right: Heke min bizaniba, min ê bigota.
mistakes.note: Irrealis conditional clauses require the irrealis suffix -ba in both protasis and apodosis.
Optative regret takes the past subjunctive (bûma), not the present indicative copula (heme).

quiz.question: Select the correct verb to complete: 'Heke me pere hebûna, me ev xanî ___.' (we would have bought)
quiz.explanation: The counterfactual apodosis requires the past subjunctive irrealis form 'bikiriya'.

quiz.question: Complete the wish: 'Xwezî em ___!' (I wish we had known!)
quiz.explanation: 'Xwezî' takes the past irrealis subjunctive ending with -ba- and 1st person plural -na: 'bizanibana'.

quiz.question: What is the primary marker of counterfactual conditionals attached to past stems?
quiz.explanation: The suffix/particle -ba is the core irrealis conditional marker in Kurmanji past hypotheticals.

quiz.question: Choose the correctly formed sentence for: 'If she had phoned, I would have answered.'
options: Heke wê telefon bikira, min ê bersiv bida.
Heke ew telefon bike, ez ê bibersivînim.
Heke wê telefon kir, min bersiv da.
Heke wê telefon dikir, min ê bersiv dabû.
quiz.explanation: Both clauses correctly utilize past subjunctive forms ending in -ba ('bikira' and 'bida').

tip: In the apodosis (result clause), Kurmanji often includes the future clitic particle 'ê' before the verb (e.g. min ê bikira) to reinforce hypothetical outcome.

title: Ezafe-Linked Relative Clauses and Resumptive Pronouns
subtitle: Connecting subordinate clauses using yê ku, ya ku, yên ku and resumptive clitics
keyPoint: Relative clauses start with an Ezafe-marker plus ku, requiring resumptive pronouns in the dependent clause when modifying oblique positions.

cells: Mirovê yê ku min ew dît...
Jina ya ku te name jê re şand...
The woman to whom you sent a letter...
Zarokên yên ku em bi wan re axivîn...
The children with whom we spoke...
Mala ku em tê de dijîn...
The house in which we live...

useCases.label: Subject Relatives
useCases.example: Ew xwendekarê ku duh hat hevalê min e.

useCases.label: Prepositional Resumption
useCases.example: Mirovê ku min jê hez dikir çû Ewropayê.

useCases.label: Possessive Resumption
useCases.example: Nivîskarê ku pirtûka wî hat wergerandin li vir e.

examples.en: Jina ku te jê re kulîlk kirîn kî ye?
Ew hevalên ku me bi wan re nan xwar hatin.
Pirtûka ku ez li ser wê difikirim gelek girîng e.
Zarokê ku dê û bavê wî çûne bajêr digirî.
Ew xaniyê ku em tê de mezin bûn pir kevn e.

mistakes.note: Past transitive clauses inside relative clauses still preserve ergative alignment (min dît).

mistakes.wrong: Jina ku ez pê re dipeyivîm bê deng ma jina ku...
mistakes.right: Jina ku ez pê re peyivîm bêdeng ma.
mistakes.note: Do not repeat the head noun at the end of the relative clause.

mistakes.wrong: Mala ku em dijîn xweş e.
mistakes.right: Mala ku em tê de dijîn xweş e.
mistakes.note: A resumptive prepositional phrase (tê de = in it) is required when the relative clause refers to an oblique location.

quiz.question: Choose the feminine singular relative marker: 'The woman who arrived' -> 'Jina ___ hat.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular heads take the feminine demonstrative Ezafe 'ya ku' (or simply the suffix '-a ku').

quiz.question: Identify the resumptive pronoun element in: 'Ew mirovê ku min jê re got...'
quiz.explanation: 'jê re' (to him/her) is the resumptive prepositional pronoun referring back to 'mirovê'.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly translates 'The students whom we teach'?
options: Xwendekarên ku em wan fêr dikin.
Xwendekarên ku em fêr dikin wan.
Xwendekaran ku em wan fêr dikin.
quiz.explanation: 'Xwendekarên ku' takes plural agreement and the resumptive clitic pronoun 'wan' before the verb.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank with the correct resumptive pronoun: 'Ew nivîsgeha ku ez ___ dixebitim.' (in which I work)
quiz.explanation: 'tê de' (in it) is the standard resumptive prepositional phrase for location inside something.

tip: Unlike English, which easily drops relative prepositions ('the place I live in'), Kurmanji almost always demands the resumptive pronoun clitic ('tê de', 'jê re', 'pê re') inside the subordinate clause.
